'''Olga Anatolevna Kocharovskaya''' ({{langx|ru|Ольга Анатольевна Кочаровская}}) is a distinguished professor of physics at [[Texas A&M University]],<ref name="cv" /> known for her contributions to [[laser physics]], [[quantum optics]]<ref name="lamb">{{cite web|url=https://www.lambaward.org/1998/index.html|title=The Willis E. Lamb Award for Laser Science and Quantum Optics|access-date=1 December 2019}}</ref> and [[gamma ray]] modulation.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://physicsworld.com/cws/article/news/2014/mar/20/gamma-ray-shaping-could-lead-to-nuclear-quantum-computers|title=Gamma-ray shaping could lead to 'nuclear' quantum computers|work=PhysicsWorld|date=20 March 2014|publisher=Institute of Physics|access-date=1 December 2019}}</ref>

== Education ==
Kocharovskaya earned a doctorate in 1986 from [[N. I. Lobachevsky State University of Nizhny Novgorod]].<ref name="cv">{{cite web|url=https://physics.tamu.edu/docs/cv/olga.pdf|title=Curriculum vitae|access-date=1 December 2019}}</ref> Her research at that time was the first to study [[electromagnetically induced transparency]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.science.tamu.edu/news/story.php?story_ID=311|title=Texas A&M University Physicists Have Devised A Way To Stop Light|date=January 26, 2001|work=Science|publisher=Texas A&M University|access-date=1 December 2019}}</ref>

== Research and career ==
Kocharovskaya began her postdoctoral research at the Institute of Applied Physics [[Russian Academy of Sciences]] in 1986, where she became a senior scientist in 1992 and group leader in 1996.<ref name="cv" />  From 1990 to 1996, she was also a visiting research scientist at the [[Université libre de Bruxelles]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=2019-09-30|title=Olga Kocharovskaya - Faculty Member|url=https://physics.tamu.edu/directory/olga-kocharovskaya/|access-date=2020-06-13|website=TAMU Physics & Astronomy|language=en-US}}</ref>  She completed a [[habilitation]] thesis titled "''Lasers without population inversion''" in 1996, awarded by the [[Commission of the Russian Federation for UNESCO|Commission of the Russian Federation.]]<ref name="cv" /><ref>{{cite web|title=Лазеры без инверсии населенностей|trans-title=Lasers without population inversion; record of Kocharovskaya's habilitation thesis|url=http://search.rsl.ru/ru/record/01000199668|access-date=1 December 2019|publisher=Russian State Library|language=ru}}</ref> In 1998, she joined [[Texas A&M University]] as an associate professor, and became a distinguished professor in 2006. Her theses have been cited in over 6000 works.

== Awards and honours ==
Kocharovskaya received the Outstanding Young Professor of the Russian Federation Award of the Russian Academy of Science in 1996, and was one of three inaugural winners of the Willis E. Lamb Award for Laser Science and Quantum Optics in 1998, sponsored by the annual Physics of Quantum Electronics conference.<ref name="lamb" /> She has also been a recipient of the University Distinguished Professor Award (2011) and the Distinguished Scientist Award from ''[[Sigma Xi]],'' the Scientific Research Society at [[Texas A&M University]] (2012).<ref>{{Cite web|date=2012-05-04|title=Two Physics Faculty Honored by Texas A&M Sigma Xi Chapter|url=https://science.tamu.edu/news/2012/05/two-physics-faculty-honored-by-texas-am-sigma-xi-chapter/|access-date=2020-06-13|website=Texas A&M College of Science|language=en-US}}</ref>

She received the [[American Physical Society]] [[Norman F. Ramsey Prize in Atomic, Molecular and Optical Physics, and in Precision Tests of Fundamental Laws and Symmetries]] (2023)<ref>{{cite web|title=2023 Norman F. Ramsey Prize in Atomic, Molecular and Optical Physics, and in Precision Tests of Fundamental Laws and Symmetries Recipient|url=https://aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?first_nm=Olga&last_nm=Kocharovskaya&year=2023|access-date=29 January 2023|publisher=[[American Physical Society]]}}</ref> and the Herbert Walther Award (2024).<ref>{{cite news |title=Olga Kocharovskaya Named 2024 Herbert Walther Award Recipient |url=https://www.optica.org/about/newsroom/news_releases/2023/november/olga_kocharovskaya_named_2024_herbert_walther_award_recipient/ |access-date=9 April 2024 |publisher=Optica |date=16 November 2023}}</ref> She has been a fellow of the [[Optical Society of America|Optical Society]] since 1997,<ref>{{cite news |title=Olga Kocharovskaya |url=https://www.optica.org/history/biographies/bios/olga_kocharovskaya/ |access-date=9 April 2024 |publisher=Optica |date=15 November 2023}}</ref> and of the APS since 2005.<ref>{{cite web|title=APS Fellows Nominated by the Division of Atomic, Molecular & Optical Physics for 2005|url=https://www.aps.org/units/damop/fellowship/index.cfm?year=2005|access-date=1 December 2019|publisher=[[American Physical Society]]}}</ref>
